name: Bidhaawyeet Latin <-> Arabic script map (Wedekind pedagogical convention)
source: Klaus & Charlotte Wedekind and Abuzeinab Musa, Beja Pedagogical Grammar (Aswan 2004 - Asmara 2005), Table 1 'Transcriptions and Pronunciation' (PDF p. 7-8) and the Arabic-script transliterations throughout the book. File in vault: Research/Beja_Pedagogical_Grammar.pdf

silentE.rule: A single 'e' between a consonant and 'h' is silent (deh, teh, seh, keh, geh). It only shows that the letters are separate (d+h, not retroflex dh). It is not written in Arabic script, because Arabic already writes these sounds with different letters.

vowels.comment: Seat = how a vowel is written depending on where it is. 'initial' = start of word; 'afterHamza' = right after an apostrophe; 'medial' = after a consonant inside the word; 'final' = last sound of the word. Marks shown here are dropped in 'plain' mode.

hamza.comment: Latin apostrophe = glottal stop. Before a vowel it takes that vowel's 'afterHamza' seat: 'a -> أَ, 'aa -> آ, 'i -> إِ, 'ii -> إي, 'u -> ءُ, 'uu -> ءُو, 'ee -> ئێ, 'oo -> ؤۆ. A final 'a is written أه (oond'a -> ۆندأه). Before a consonant or at the end of a word: ء.

gemination: A doubled consonant is written once with shadda (assaa -> أَسّا). A doubled gw or kw is written out twice, as the book does (sikwkwart -> سِكْوكْوَرت).

notInSource.comment: Characters the Pedagogical Grammar does not cover. They are added so that no input fails. The single vowels e and o occur only in a few loanwords and in Vanhove spellings; they are written like ee and oo, and that change cannot be undone when converting back.
notInSource.e: same as ee (ێ); silent between a consonant and h

addedForReversibility.comment: Not in the Pedagogical Grammar. Added in 'full' mode only, so that Arabic can be turned back into exactly the same Latin spelling. 'plain' mode removes them.
addedForReversibility.finalH: A word-final consonant h gets sukun: baruuh -> بَرٌوهْ (otherwise a final ه reads as the -a ending).
addedForReversibility.consonantalYW: y or w with no vowel after them gets sukun when it follows a consonant or a short i/u: hidy -> هِديْ, eetyhami -> ێتيْهَمے (otherwise ي/و reads as long ii/uu).
addedForReversibility.vowelHiatus: Two vowels in a row with no apostrophe are written as if there were one (uugin'a-inriib -> ...أَإِ...); converting back adds the apostrophe.
